chosen.title: The Termination Algorithm: How 'Token Consumption' Became a Layoff Metric
chosen.rationale: A live July 2026 lawsuit against Meta alleges the company used AI-usage proxies like token consumption to target employees for layoffs, and industry-wide, AI-generated performance data is now used in discipline and termination decisions without human review — a concrete, breaking-news instance of the algorithmic-management critique Dawn's beat is built for, with a real corporate defendant and paper trail rather than a hypothetical.

sources.name: CNBC via Mintz AI Washington Report

rejected_candidates.title: The Lobby in the Room: How the AI Industry Wrote Its Own Rulebook
rejected_candidates.rationale: A newly published ACM FAccT 2026 paper documents that AI corporations and trade groups now account for over 80% of AI-related lobbying, actively steering regulation toward 'technical symptoms' instead of economic incentives — a direct, freshly-peer-reviewed case study in Dawn's core beat of corporate capture of public institutions and the Naomi-Klein-style 'follow the money' argument.

sources.name: ACM FAccT 2026 — Big AI's Regulatory Capture

rejected_candidates.title: Your Camera Roll Is the Product: Consent, AI, and the New Surveillance Default
rejected_candidates.rationale: Reporting this month shows consumer apps like Tinder moving to let AI scan a user's entire camera roll, arriving as the US still has no federal law meaningfully limiting this kind of data harvesting — a timely, visceral entry point into Dawn's surveillance-capitalism and data-colonialism beat that lands the abstraction in something readers already carry in their pocket.
